subcmd.trust: Trust a project folder so its .env, hooks and coder policy load (--list, --revoke)
wstrust.prompt.title:
This folder is not a trusted workspace: %s
It contains project configuration that ChatCLI has NOT loaded:
wstrust.prompt.explain: These files can run commands on this machine, change where your API keys and tokens are sent, or loosen the coder's permissions. Trust the folder only if you trust its author.
wstrust.prompt.question: Trust this folder and load them? [y/N]
wstrust.prompt.store_failed: Could not save the trust decision (%v); it applies to this run only.
wstrust.prompt.declined: Project configuration of %s was not loaded for this run. To trust it later: chatcli trust %s
wstrust.warn.untrusted: chatcli: warning: %s is not a trusted workspace, so its project configuration was ignored: %s. To trust it: chatcli trust %s
wstrust.cli.usage: Usage: chatcli trust [dir] | chatcli trust --revoke [dir] | chatcli trust --list
wstrust.cli.flag_list: list trusted workspaces and whether their trust is still current
wstrust.cli.flag_revoke: revoke the trust of the folder
wstrust.cli.no_files: No project configuration files are present yet. Adding one revokes this trust until you confirm again.
wstrust.policy.untrusted: Local policy %s ignored: the workspace is not trusted (chatcli trust).
wstrust.policy.allow_ignored: Local policy %s: %d allow rule(s) ignored. A project policy can only add ask or deny rules.
wstrust.tls.insecure: chatcli: WARNING: TLS certificate verification is DISABLED (%s=true). Anyone on the network path can read your API keys and tokens. Unset it and set CHATCLI_CA_BUNDLE to your corporate CA instead.
wstrust.history.legacy: Reading the previous prompt history from %s; new entries go to %s. Delete the old file once you no longer need it.
